checks.name: console_receipt_order
checks.scope: Actual ConsoleStore from the production frontend runs in a Node VM without DOM or a WebView2/native owner. Message order matches legal bounded-ACK publisher scheduling; no browser or Windows execution claimed.

bugs.condition: A matching snapshot can arrive before the operation receipt, including rapid round-trip edits and a bounded native ACK batch.
bugs.before: The pending record was deleted solely because its value matched the state. A later failure or a stricter success revision was ignored.
bugs.after: Pending state can be resolved by a snapshot only after the exact request has a successful ACK; existing sequence/generation and required revision gates remain.

bugs.condition: Focusing a text editor owns a draft even if no value was changed; close-check counted every draft as unsubmitted.
bugs.before: Closing could warn about abandoned edits after focusing an unchanged field.
bugs.after: Close inquiry counts only differing drafts on current certified pages; pending requests, unknown ownership and retired pages stay protected. No draft mutation, implicit submission or native close policy change. Each referenced page is indexed once.

notes: The existing large-state test now includes the explicit successful ACK required by the production protocol. It still checks that an unrelated editing draft is retained.
These are two functional state-flow fixes; the 24 cases are not 24 distinct bugs.
No version, build, packaging, Notebook, INDEX, cursor, shared INI store or native adapter changes were made by this task.
